instructions: Put the 1 oz dried wood ears in a large bowl and cover them with plenty of warm water. Soak for 30 minutes. They'll swell to about four times their size and turn soft and floppy.
Meanwhile, bring a medium pot of water to a boil.
Drain the wood ears and rinse them well, rubbing off any grit. Cut off the hard knobs where they grew on the log and tear any big pieces into bite-size ones. That should be about 4 cups.
Add the wood ears to the boiling water and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're tender but still have a crunch.
Drain them and rinse under cold running water until they're cool. Let them drain well, then pat them dry with a clean towel.
In a large bowl, stir the garlic, 1 1/2 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp sesame oil until the sugar dissolves.
Add the wood ears and toss until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, thinly slice 2 of the green onions.
Seed the red chili, chop it finely and put it in a small bowl.
Stir the salad again to bring up the dressing from the bottom. Transfer it to a plate and scatter the green onions over the top.
Serve cold with the chopped chili on the side.
method_notes: The Woks of Life (the lead) and Omnivore's Cookbook both soak dried wood ears, boil them 3 to 4 minutes, cool them in cold water and dress them with garlic, black vinegar, light soy sauce and a little sugar. The Woks of Life finishes with sesame oil and chills the salad 30 minutes; Omnivore's Cookbook pours hot Sichuan peppercorn oil over the dressing instead, so this follows the lead. Both add fresh red chili to the bowl; here it's served on the side so the salad stays mild. Cilantro, an optional garnish in both, is left out.
